messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p95 SLO breach detected on /v1/generate (us-west-2). p95=1420ms > threshold=1200ms. Automatic regional fallback triggered (policy: prod-global). Routing engine initiated reroute to us-east-1, ~40% traffic shifted. Observed oscillation: reroute -> recovery -> revert -> reroute. Pager sent to oncall. See runbook: https://runbooks.internal/routing/p95-oscillation

maria (oncall): ack. I'm on it. @devon can you pull routing logs and check variant mapping?

devon: looking now. seeing rapid "decide_reroute" events in router logs:

```
routing-engine: decide_reroute route=default region=us-west-2 p95_ms=1420 threshold_ms=1200 action=reroute -> us-east-1
routing-engine: decide_reroute route=default region=us-east-1 p95_ms=1100 threshold_ms=1200 action=restore -> us-west-2
routing-engine: decide_reroute route=default region=us-west-2 p95_ms=1505 threshold_ms=1200 action=reroute -> us-east-1
```

Also seeing model mismatch warnings in us-east-1: "model_variant v2-quant decoding_latency high for seq_len ~512".

maria (oncall): interesting — could be that v2-quant rollout in us-east-1 is slower for our common seq lengths, pushing p95 over threshold and triggering the thermostat. If fallback sends traffic back to west and west has the 'expected' variant, that flipflops. Hypothesis: aggressive threshold + no/hardly any hysteresis on the policy.

ryan: I can temporarily disable region-level fallback for prod-global to stop the oscillation. That will keep traffic in originating region until we fix variant. Thoughts?

samantha: confirmed: v2-quant has a slower attention kernel for mid-sized sequences on T4-style instances we've got in us-east-1 right now. It slips p95 by ~200-300ms on certain prompts. We should pin to v2-fp16 until we reprofile.

maria (oncall): plan then: 1) devon -> pin default route in us-east-1 to v2-fp16 for 30m 2) ryan -> disable region fallback on prod-global temporarily 3) samantha -> prepare immediate rollback of v2-quant rollout 4) nate -> draft customer-facing impact note. Execute and update here. :rotating_light:

devon: executing pin now. command: 

```
# pin route to variant in control plane
curl -s -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routes/pin \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"route":"default","region":"us-east-1","model_variant":"v2-fp16","duration_ms":1800000}'
```

and patching policy hysteresis:

```
PATCH /api/v1/routing/policies/prod-global
{ "p95_threshold_ms": 1200, "hysteresis_ms": 300000 }
```

Pinned & policy patched: controlplane -> 200 OK. Verified via /debug/routing-matrix: default@us-east-1 -> v2-fp16 (pinned).

incident-bot: NOTE: automatic re-enable of regional fallback scheduled (in 60m) unless canceled.

maria (oncall): monitoring. Current metrics: us-east-1 p95 dropped from 1420ms -> 980ms within 1 min of pin. No further reroutes in last 2 cycles. Good sign.

nate: drafting customer note: "We experienced routing instability impacting ~10% of requests between 15:03–15:15 UTC. We implemented a mitigation (pinned model variant and adjusted routing policy) and service performance returned to normal. Engineering is investigating root cause and will follow up with timeline and permanent fix." Want me to post to status.redwood.ai?

maria (oncall): please post draft to status and include CI ticket link once created. :white_check_mark:

samantha: starting rollback of v2-quant rollout in us-east-1 now. Also kicking off a perf job to reproduce seq_len distribution seen in prod; will attach profiler traces.

ryan: disabled region fallback on prod-global. Confirmed via policy audit log. Also temporarily scaled up the dedicated pool in us-east-1 by 1 instance to reduce queueing while we stabilize.

devon: monitoring dashboard shows steady p95 in both regions now. There was one minor blip but control plane did not reroute. Handoff will remain with oncall for 30m, then we reassess.

maria (oncall): root cause summary (prelim): an aggressive p95 threshold combined with insufficient hysteresis in prod-global routing policy plus a partially rolled out model variant (v2-quant) that regresses performance for common sequence lengths caused oscillatory reroutes between regions.

mitigations applied: pinned route->v2-fp16 in us-east-1 (30m), increased hysteresis to 5m, disabled regional fallback for prod-global, rolled back v2-quant rollout in us-east-1, scaled dedicated pool +1 instance.

follow-ups/tickets:
- DEVOPS-3421: add thermostat hysteresis guardrails and min-stable-window for p95-triggered reroutes.
- ML-1290: perf/regression tests for quantized variants across common seq_len distributions.
- CTRLPL-881: expose "pin until" UI and force-unpin audit entry.

nate: posted status update (link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2012345678) and notified top 5 affected customers via email template.

samantha: attaching profiler summary in the ticket. initial note: quant kernel slower at seq_len 256–1024, median latency +220ms.

maria (oncall): handoff at 15:45 UTC -> staying oncall until 21:00 UTC. If oscillation resumes, escalate to eng-runtime immediately. Otherwise we'll close incident after follow-ups are filed and postmortem scheduled.

devon: creating incident ticket and postmortem doc now. Will include logs, commands run, and timeline. Closing thread summary: root cause, mitigations, follow-ups (see tickets above). :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: p95 back within SLO. No active reroutes. Auto-reminders for follow-ups in 24h.

maria (oncall): thanks all. going to watch dashboards for 30m then move to postmortem. :thumbsup:
